slides.headline: Surfers: your pop-up starts on the mat
slides.sub: Where clinical Pilates fits for a smoother, stronger summer in the water.

slides.title: Pop-ups: a push and a tuck
slides.body: Getting to your feet quickly needs pressing strength, a strong trunk and hips that flex freely. Reformer planks and knee tucks train that exact sequence with adjustable spring load.

slides.title: Mid-back endurance for paddling
slides.body: Paddling asks the upper back to extend for long periods. Pilates extension work, like swan variations, builds endurance there so the neck and lower back do less of the job.

slides.title: Hip mobility for your stance
slides.body: A low, stable stance needs hips that rotate and knees that bend comfortably. Controlled hip mobility and squat variations on the reformer can help you settle into position.

slides.title: Balance for a moving board
slides.body: Single-leg work and standing on unstable surfaces train the small adjustments you make on a board. Most people notice steadier legs after a few weeks of regular practice.

slides.title: Plan sessions around the swell
slides.body: Many surfers fit one or two sessions a week around the forecast. Your program can lean towards recovery and mobility after a big week in the water.

slides.headline: Want a surf-ready program?
slides.body: Our Pilates team starts with an assessment and tailors exercises to your surfing and any niggles. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Want a quicker, smoother pop-up this summer? Some of the work happens on land.

A good pop-up is a press, a tuck and a stable landing. Clinical Pilates can train each part: reformer planks and knee tucks for the transition, extension work for paddling endurance through the upper back, hip mobility for a lower stance, and balance work for the tiny adjustments a moving board demands.

Most surfers fit one or two sessions a week around the forecast, with more recovery-focused sessions after big weeks in the water.

story.headline: Want a quicker pop-up?
story.body: Try slow plank-to-knee-tuck reps a few times a week. Strength and control make getting to your feet smoother.
